obs: "This regulation was obviously intended to supplement 194 of the Criminal Code . . . by supplying the detail which Congress contemplated should be so supplied when it left undefined or other authorized depository for mail matter."; "That 194 contemplates that its general language shall be made definite by such order is plain"
Addison v. Holly Hill Fruit Products, Inc.
“But when Congress wants to give wide discretion it uses broad language.”
Federal Communications Commission v. WNCN Listeners Guild

"It is common ground that the Act does not define the term public interest, convenience, and necessity. The Court has characterized the public-interest standard of the Act as a supple instrument for the exercise of discretion by the expert body which Congress has charged to carry out its legislative policy."
Securities Industry Ass'n v. Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

"Indeed, the relevant statutory language does not specify any factors that the Board must consider in making that determination. The general nature of the statutory language, therefore, suggests that Congress vested the Board with considerable discretion to consider and weigh a variety of factors"
